stem: Which of the following is an equivalent form of the equation \(y = x^{2} + 6x + 1\) in which the coordinates of the vertex of its graph in the \(xy\)-plane appear as constants?

explanation.B: Incorrect. \((x + 3)^{2}\) already includes \(+9\), which must be subtracted; this expands to \(x^{2} + 6x + 10\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. The sign inside the square is wrong; \((x - 3)^{2}\) gives \(-6x\), not \(+6x\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This adds \(9\) instead of subtracting it; it expands to \(x^{2} + 6x + 19\).

verify:
x = symbols('x')
rhs = {k: value(v.split('=')[1]) for k, v in choices.items()}
ok = [k for k in rhs if simplify(rhs[k] - (x**2 + 6*x + 1)) == 0]
assert ok == [answer]
